runs.name: WEC Energy Group, Inc.; NYSE WEC, SEC CIK 0000783325, formerly Wisconsin Energy Corporation, renamed on acquiring Integrys 2015-06-29; Milwaukee utility holding company, regulated electricity and gas in Wisconsin and the Upper Peninsula, gas distribution in Illinois, Minnesota and Michigan, about 60% of ATC, We Power and WECI, six reportable segments; a $3.0B at-the-market program with forwards 2025-10-31; Point Beach power purchase agreement signed 2026-08-14 pending PSCW approval; the 10-K names no rival, Alliant, Xcel and CMS chosen as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.box: OUT AT Q7, ON THE FLOOR
runs.entry: The v5 re-run order, unattended work-hours cycle, one dispatched analyst under the canonical brief, from scratch. The brief's departures: the repository path after the move of 2026-10-25; the lines of evidence and the competitors derived by the analyst from the FY2025 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7. Price **$111.12** (close 2026-10-26, aggregator, flagged) x **325,849,383 shares** (10-Q cover for the period ended 2026-06-30, accession 0000783325-26-000087, read by hand: cover_shares.py parsed no count; 6,392,021 shares sold forward and unsettled beside) = cap **$36,208M**; sovereign **5.31%** (Treasury 30-year par, 2026-10-26). **Q1 IN** (a regulated return on approved capital in four states, allowed returns and a $37.5B 2026-2030 capital plan published). **Q2 IN on the deciding part, Wisconsin** (54.2% of the positive parts of five-year segment net income; territories by state law, indeterminate permits, no retail-choice bill; the regulator-set return carried to Q3); Illinois (12%) narrowing: Peoples Gas pipe spending paused November 2023, capital disallowed 2023 and 2024, a $205M Attorney General settlement. The 10-K names no rival, Alliant, Xcel and CMS chosen as a CONVENTION of the run: average ROE 2016 to 2025 WEC 11.7%, Alliant 11.0%, Xcel 10.4%, CMS 13.8% (with a 2021 bank-sale gain); WEC about two points above its 9.80% Wisconsin allowed return, helped by holding-company debt. **Q3 weighs against narrowly** ($11.4B more capital 2020 to 2025 for about $579M more pre-tax operating earnings, about 5.1%; spending compulsory and about to double, $5.0B, $6.9B, $7.0B for 2026 to 2028 against depreciation of about $1.5B). **Q4 IN, weighs against** (adjusted EPS featured two years running over recurring Illinois charges; 2025 adjusted EPS $5.27 at the top of guidance). **Q5 integrity IN** (the Illinois matters disputes over cost recovery, not findings of dishonesty), ability weighs for in Wisconsin. **Q6 weighs against in both parts** (dividend about 74% of earnings while shares are sold through a $3.0B at-the-market program with forwards; share purchases only to supply plans, above the Q7 bottom, written back; the 2025 bonus paid 200% on adjusted EPS excluding the $205M charge, GAAP EPS $4.81 below the lowest band, the cash-flow target about $725M below the outcome). **Q7 OUT, on the floor and above the top of the range**: owner cash equity-only 2021 to 2025, $1,452M a year after maintenance literal, **$1,288M central** with production tax credits taken out and their ten-year value added back (a CONVENTION of the run, the five-year average over ten years), -$734M after all spending, negative every year; growth shown 16.6% cut to sales growth of 4.19% under (f); growth spending $1,452M in year one to $2,101M in year ten; utility debt credit $792M a year at the 47% cap (the PSCW allowed debt share), binding below $1,560M a year of long-term debt raised; the growth case the bottom. Value range **$67.70 to $78.29 a share equity-only (central)**; 3.56% at the price, none earning the 5.31% sovereign; **fair price $33.14 equity-only, central**, all-equity -$29.34, not positive; beside: literal window $35.91, base without 2021 $36.96, forwards settled $34.69. Facts after the stop recorded, not weighed. Balance sheet: assets up 71% and equity 57% 2016 to 2025; total debt about $10.2B to $22.3B, about 53% to 62% of debt plus common equity; pre-tax interest coverage 4.4x (2022) to 2.9x (2025); goodwill flat at $3.05B from Integrys; current liabilities exceed current assets by $2.3B. Strongest evidence against, as the analyst put it: owner cash after all spending negative every year, a capital plan larger than the market value, about 5% pre-tax on added capital, Illinois as regulatory erosion in miniature, maximum bonuses on a figure that excludes the loss, a price that returns less than the bond. Framework gaps for the operator: the debt-credit cap without rate base by company (the Wisconsin 47% used for the whole); production tax credits under Whose tax and their schedule by project; run.py missing acquisitions and ATC contributions in capital spending; cover_shares.py parsing no count. Could not get: rate base by company, the credit schedule by project, rivals' cash flows on a common tag (CMS capex 2023 to 2025 missing), so the peer comparison is by ROE only. Ordering departure declared by the analyst: the Q6 buyback line cited the Q7 bottom in the commit before Q7's own. Analyst's commits: pathspec commits of its own paths, last `c3bb85ad`. Dispatcher's check: check_framework PASS; 130 id citations resolve, no E-ids, no citation slip, 30 adjacent fragment pairs checked, five checker mispairings resolved by hand (M2000-037, M2002-092, M2018-055 and L2016-006 quotes read beside the preceding id; one filing quote beside M1995-038; `dispatcher_cite_check.py`); no tracked research file over 200 KB. Contamination declared: a VST run file name and folder in a directory listing, VST and ARCB commit subjects and git status, one memory index line; none used. Position note filled at the fold: not held. Armed at the equity-only fair price.
runs.narr: OUT at Q7 on the floor: a Wisconsin-centred electric and gas utility holding company, the castle standing on state franchises, but owner cash is negative after all spending every year, the capital plan exceeds the market value and the central case returns 3.56% at the price; value range $67.70 to $78.29 equity-only against $111.12. Fair $33.14 equity-only, central; all-equity -$29.34, not positive; armed.
